desc:
The string s consists of the characters '(', ')' and '?'. You must replace every '?' by either '(' or ')'. A resulting string is well-formed when every '(' is closed by a later ')', every ')' closes an earlier '(', and nothing stays open.

Return the number of different ways to replace the question marks so that the result is well-formed, modulo 1,000,000,007. Two ways are different if some '?' receives a different character.

For example, "(??)" has 2 ways ("(())" and "()()"), and "????" also has 2.
hints: A string is well-formed exactly when its running balance never goes below 0 and ends at 0. So the only thing that matters after a prefix is the current balance.
Let ways[b] be the number of ways to fill the prefix read so far so that the balance is b and was never negative. Update it for one new character at a time.
For '(', every balance moves up by one; for ')' it moves down by one (balance 0 dies); for '?' both happen and the counts add up. The answer is ways[0] after the last character.
editorial: This is a counting DP over (position, balance). Let dp[b] be the number of valid prefix fillings that end with balance b. Starting with dp = [1] (balance 0), read the characters one by one and build a new array: a '(' contributes new[b+1] += dp[b], a ')' contributes new[b-1] += dp[b] for b ≥ 1, and '?' does both. Everything is taken modulo 109+7.

The balance never exceeds n/2 in a useful state, since it must still come back to 0, and an odd length has no valid filling at all. With n states per step the DP runs in O(n2) time and O(n) space, which is fine for n ≤ 1,000. As a sanity check, a string of only '?' of length 2m gives the Catalan number Cm.
